rows.title: The Nearest Star Is One You Can't See (And It Has a Planet)
rows.line1: How far is the nearest star? Proxima Centauri, a small red dwarf 4.24 light-years away, is so faint you can never see it without a telescope. Even light, the fastest thing there is, takes more than four years to cross the gap.

rows.title: Earth Is Losing Its Spin (And the Moon Is Taking It)
rows.line1: Right now, in Britain, the ground is carrying you east at about a thousand kilometres an hour, and you feel nothing. What if Earth stopped spinning? A sudden stop is a thought experiment: the air would keep going. The real story is that Earth is already slowing down, and the clocks have been keeping score.

rows.title: What Happens When a Star Enters Our Solar System?
rows.line1: Gliese 710 is an orange dwarf star heading towards the Solar System. In about 1.3 million years, its predicted journey through the distant Oort Cloud could reshape the comet traffic around the Sun — while staying far beyond the planets.

rows.title: What Happens When Earth's Magnetic Field Flips?
rows.line1: Why is Earth's north magnetic pole racing towards Siberia, and what would a magnetic field reversal mean for the world beneath it?

rows.title: Is Betelgeuse About to Explode?
rows.line1: Betelgeuse is a dying red supergiant star on the shoulder of Orion. When it dimmed by more than 60 per cent in late 2019, astronomers wondered whether it was preparing to go supernova — and what our sky will look like when it finally explodes.
